description:
This high-resolution satellite map displays detailed land cover classifications in a rural or semi-natural area, likely in Europe (eastern Germany or Hungary, based on document context), using a false-colour infrared composite where red/magenta indicates vegetation and dark green/blue represents water. The base imagery has a resolution of 2.5 metres, consistent with Spot 5 data from approximately 2010–2011.

The map features several polygons, outlined in thin dark lines, each associated with a four-digit Copernicus Land Monitoring Service (CLMS) land cover class code. A prominent dark green linear feature, identified as a watercourse (river or canal), is classified with the code "8110". According to the accompanying document, this code represents "Natural & semi-natural water courses" or Riparian Zone (RZ) data.

Adjacent to the watercourse are narrow, elongated yellow/orange polygons labelled "1620". Based on the surrounding text, these represent "Lines of trees and shrub" or Small Woody Features (SWF), which are typically 10 m to 25 m in width and have a Minimum Mapping Unit (MMU) of 0.5 ha, appearing within urban or agricultural areas. Other surrounding land cover includes larger red/magenta polygons classified as "3110" (likely Broad-leaved forest), "4100" (likely Grassland), and a partially visible "2110" (likely Arable land). No explicit scale bar, compass, or legend is present within the image itself.
